title: Which part of the tail term carries the calibrated gain: the weight on precipitation, or the threshold?
origin: evaluation/calibration_test_plan.json passed for variant C (no threshold): calibrated Brier at 20 mm, tailC2000 minus control2000, -0.00154 [-0.00218, -0.00100] on the test year. The original tail arm (hard threshold at 20 mm, full dose) showed no such gain at step 3000 (+1.3 percent, interval across zero). On the validation period, D (soft 5 mm) and E (no threshold, a third of C's dose) gained after calibration as C did. This plan scores every step-2000 variant on the test year by the same rule, to see whether the gain follows the threshold.

models.tail2000: original tail arm, hard threshold 20 mm, weight 13 716, step 2000: ~/bris-models/tail/tail-step002000_inference.ckpt
models.tailE2000: no threshold, weight 13.03 (a third of C's)
models.tailC2000: no threshold, weight 39.09; already scored, repeated here for the table only

test: exactly as evaluation/calibration_test_plan.json: 2025-08-01..2026-09-06, every day, 4 members, BRIS_LEADTIMES=7, +30 h daily totals, strict common cases of the variant, control2000 and MEPS, scripts/hits_and_calibration.py --cv month --replicates 5000 --meps, each variant scored as its own pair against control2000. Forecasts may be split into date chunks across jobs; the dates and datasets per day are unchanged.

endpoint_per_variant.measure: Brier score at 20 mm after month-out isotonic calibration, variant minus control2000
endpoint_per_variant.uncertainty: paired block bootstrap, seven-day blocks, 5000 replicates

registered_prediction.hypothesis: the calibrated gain comes from extra weight on precipitation below 20 mm; a hard 20 mm threshold, which gives the term nothing to say about days below it, carries none
registered_prediction.tailB2000: better or no difference: its hard threshold is at 5 mm, so the term still acts on most heavy-rain days
registered_prediction.supported_if: D and E better, and neither A nor tail2000 better
registered_prediction.contradicted_if: A or tail2000 better, or D and E both not better

secondary_reported: raw Brier, ROC area, hits and false alarms per variant
dose within no-threshold arms: E (a third of the dose) against C, read from their separate differences against control2000, not tested
scripts/station_extremes.py per variant against control2000 (exploratory, as that script is)
not_claimed: Seven comparisons on one test year, one training draw each, at step 2000. Read as a pattern across variants, not as seven independent findings.
